name: LegoBot
target_anatomy: neurovascular (diagnostic angiography, aspiration thrombectomy); coronary and peripheral stated as applicable
devices_driven: guidewire 0.014 in; 2.8 Fr/0.028 in microcatheter; 5 Fr angiographic catheter; 6 Fr aspiration catheter; 8 Fr guide catheter (five off-the-shelf devices tested for buckling load)
rotation_detail: clamped-wheel rotation: hollow-shaft direct-drive motor (0.9 N.m peak) turns the clamped instrument; module coupler adds a second torque input via bevel gears; decoupled from translation by command compensation
footprint_mm: 345 x 249 x 115 (three modules, Fig. 6a); module 190 mm wide
force_sensing: motor side only (current, dual 17-bit encoders); no direct instrument sensing (stated limitation)
haptics_leader: none; Xbox gamepad teleoperation; haptic feedback not yet implemented
sterility: not validated (stated future work); preloaded replaceable modules; standard Luer lock / Y-connector interfaces
validation_detail: benchtop: 8 Fr catheter slip test; buckling-load test with 5 devices; silicone neurovascular phantom (Type III arch): angiography with 2 modules and aspiration thrombectomy with 3 modules (clot aspirated); one demonstration each, repeat counts N.R.; one timed module exchange 1 min 50 s
key_numbers: peak insertion force 5.3 N and torque 8.4 mN.m (8 Fr) vs requirement 4.5 N / 8 mN.m; buckling load 0.1 N (0.014 in wire) to 4.3 N (8 Fr); coupler: 5 full microcatheter rotations vs ~180 deg without; 500 Hz command loop; 345x249x115 mm for 3 instruments vs 360x250x250 mm (2 instruments) of Kantu per Table I
